A conversation with Terri (48) from Jamaica.
sentences.Terri Senior fra Jamaica har alltid vært: Terri Senior from Jamaica has always been interested in the world around her, and she has studied in Venezuela, the USA and the Netherlands.
She has also lived in Iceland.
sentences.Nå har Terri bodd i Norge siden 1995, og: Terri has lived in Norway since 1995, and she currently works for the Red Cross.
sentences.Hun forteller ivrig om erfaringene sine: She talks eagerly about her experiences in a fine Sunnmøre dialect.
sentences.Har det vært slik helt siden du kom til: Has it been like that ever since you came to Norway?
sentences.Ja, jeg har alltid vært veldig nysgjerri: Yes, I have always been very curious, and I like to express my opinions.
sentences.Derfor har jeg vært aktiv i samfunnslive: That's why I have been active in the community and taken part in a lot of international work here in Norway.
sentences.Hva gjorde du selv for å bli integrert?: What did you yourself do to become integrated?
sentences.I begynnelsen var jeg aktiv i mye intern: At first I was active in a lot of international work in Ålesund, and I made contact with Norwegians where it was natural.
sentences.Jeg fikk både et norsk og et internasjon: I got both a Norwegian and an international network through that work.
sentences.Hva har du gjort for å bli det?: What have you done to get so good?
sentences.Jeg var ikke god i norsk i begynnelsen,: I wasn't good at Norwegian at first, but I decided to speak.
sentences.Jeg kastet meg ut i samtaler med nordmen: I threw myself into conversations with Norwegians from the first day.
sentences.Var det andre måter du lærte norsk på?: Were there other ways you learned Norwegian?
sentences.Jeg så mye på tv, mye mer enn jeg egentl: I watched a lot of TV, much more than I actually like to.
sentences.Mange programmer på tv er engelske med n: Many programmes on TV are in English with Norwegian subtitles, and so this was a great help to me.
sentences.Jeg pleier fortsatt å lese teksten på ma: I still often read the subtitles on many TV programmes.
sentences.Kan du si noe om det norske arbeidslivet: Can you say something about Norwegian working life?
sentences.Jeg synes at nordmenn er litt dårlige ti: I think Norwegians are a bit bad at using the skills of people who move here.
sentences.Personlig har jeg vært heldig, for jeg b: Personally I have been lucky, because I started working only a few months after I came to Norway.
sentences.Har du noen konkrete tips til folk som ø: Do you have any concrete tips for people who want a job?
sentences.Jeg tror det viktigste er å bruke nettve: I think the most important thing is to use your network.
sentences.Hvis du kjenner mange mennesker, er det: If you know lots of people, it is easier to find a job.
sentences.En annen ting som jeg tror på, er god, g: Another thing I believe in is good, old-fashioned contact, face to face.
sentences.Jobbsøknader og cv-er kan lett bli borte: Job applications and CVs can easily get lost in a drawer.
sentences.Derfor kan det være smart å ta direkte k: That's why it can be smart to contact workplaces directly and introduce yourself.
sentences.Hva er det typisk norske som alle må lær: What is the typically Norwegian thing that everyone has to learn?
sentences.Det er litt vanskelig for meg å vite hva: It's a bit difficult for me to know what is typically Norwegian and what is typical of a Jamaican, because I have been here in Norway for so long now, but using nature is very important.
sentences.Hvis du klarer å ha et aktivt forhold ti: If you manage to have an active relationship with the four seasons, it is good for both body and mind.
sentences.Jeg vil også si at toleranse er en vikti: I would also say that tolerance is an important value in Norway.
sentences.Alle kulturer kan lære mye av Norge når: All cultures can learn a lot from Norway when it comes to tolerance of diversity.
